Fix ETag mismatch in static assets during development

# Fix ETag mismatch in static assets during development

- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

Fix LastModified comparison precision mismatch in StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler

## Description

During development with `ReloadStaticAssetsAtRuntime` enabled, static assets always returned 200 OK with a regenerated ETag instead of the manifest ETag, breaking 304 Not Modified caching.

**Root cause:** `StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler` compared `fileInfo.LastModified` (sub-second precision) against the manifest's `LastModified` (HTTP date format, second precision only). The comparison always failed, triggering unnecessary ETag regeneration.

**Changes:**
- Add `TruncateToSeconds` helper to strip sub-second components from `DateTimeOffset`
- Apply truncation when comparing file timestamp against manifest value
- Add inline comment explaining why truncation is correct (the manifest truncates the timestamp when it serializes the Last-Modified header since HTTP date format only supports second precision)
- Add unit tests for the truncation logic

```csharp
// Before: always triggers change detection due to precision mismatch
if (fileInfo.LastModified != asset.GetLastModified())

// After: proper comparison at second precision
if (TruncateToSeconds(fileInfo.LastModified) != asset.GetLastModified())
```
